analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and adds one troubleshooting row, near head line 2316, about cold loads refused while an idle model is resident under an unexpired Autopilot placement hold. I examined both supplied head-text units (lines 416-1208), which are unchanged context, and the patch excerpt. No code, configuration, wire protocol or authorization behavior changes. The excerpt is complete.

The new row describes existing behavior. Held slots are excluded from eviction (ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots, autopilotHoldsModel) and get no free_for_load_gb reclaim credit (autopilotHeldWeightBytes), per the doc. That code is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify the claims. Nothing in the docs weakens a mitigation or invalidates a threat-model assumption.

The surrounding context touches T-041 (SSD prefix cache, SEC-035 accepted), A-001, A-016 and TB-007. Statements there, such as the coordinator-authenticated cache scope, no cache receipts for the Super slot, and the unchanged 30-minute TTL, are existing documentation and not modified by this PR.

Open question for integration: the Autopilot hold is a new availability-affecting concept (a placement hold could block cold loads), and its model-autopilot.md and source were not supplied. If that feature was introduced elsewhere in the same PR, it should be checked for the DoS and authorization implications of who can create a hold and whether it has an expiry. This doc-only change does not itself justify a finding.
